{'result': '# New hire handbook

**Document type**: initialization
**Role**: Handbook issued when you join the product R&D organisation
**Audience**: New hires

Welcome to the product engineering group. Before your career clock starts, this handbook sets out the public rules. Everything in it is part of the published game design, and you can use it for long-term planning.

## What is published

- **Published**: This handbook covers the published rules: the level ladder, visible stats, quarterly energy and main actions, the timeline and promotion windows, performance grades, risk and failure rules, and monthly pay.
- **Not published**: Not listed here. You can only infer these from emails, meeting notes, manager feedback and outcomes: promotion score thresholds, talk tiers, performance formula weights, hidden risk and random event odds.
- **Note**: You cannot see everything that is happening in the organisation. Plan across quarters and years with incomplete information.

## Levels

There are ten levels, L1 to L10. Higher levels expect broader impact and set a higher bar for promotion.

A promotion window opens every 6 months. The bar depends on Skill, Network, Output and level; the exact thresholds are hidden.

| Level | Name | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| L1 | Junior engineer | Carries out tasks with clear guidance |
| L2 | Engineer | Owns modules independently |
| L3 | Senior engineer | Owns core modules, with growing technical responsibility |
| L4 | Staff engineer | Works on critical systems with major project impact |
| L5 | Principal / team lead | Leads a subsystem or small team |
| L6 | Senior principal / tech lead | Leads large programmes or sets technical direction |
| L7 | Director of engineering | Department-level technical strategy |
| L8 | Senior director | Cross-department technical planning |
| L9 | Distinguished fellow / architecture committee | Company-wide technical influence |
| L10 | Chief architect / fellow | Makes company-wide technical decisions over a long horizon |

## Visible statistics

Shown on your panel or in the monthly summary. These are your main inputs for decisions.

| Key | Name | Range | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Health | Health | 0–10 | Physical and mental stamina. Long-term overwork wears it down |
| Dignity | Dignity | 0–10 | Self-respect and recognition at work. Staying low for too long triggers a crisis |
| Skill | Skill | 0–unbounded | Professional capability |
| Network | Network | 0–unbounded | The working relationships you can draw on |
| Level | Level | L1–L10 | Current career level |
| Output | Output | 0–unbounded | The visible results you have built up over time |
| Wealth | Wealth | unbounded | Cumulative wealth |
| Energy | Energy | 0–3 | Your energy budget for the quarter, spent on quarterly actions |
| CurrentLevelDuration | Months at current level | 0–unbounded | Consecutive months at present level |

## Time

- Length: 48 months
- Story events per month: 3
- Each month:
  - 1. A new month starts and you are paid the base salary for your level
  - 2. Up to 3 story events are drawn from the pool
  - 3. You play through the story events and make your choices
  - 4. At the end of a quarter (months 3, 6, 9…), once the month’s event quota is full, you move on to quarterly energy actions
  - 5. Allocate your 3 Energy points for the quarter. You can pick the same action more than once, until you finish or skip
  - 6. Choose one quarterly main action (or none)
  - 7. Your stats are settled. Crossing a red line may bring a written or verbal warning
  - 8. Every half year: a 1:1 with your manager (no decision needed)
  - 9. Every 6 months: formal performance review and bonus

## Energy actions

3 Energy per quarter. Unused Energy does not roll over.

- Energy each quarter: 3
- Unused Energy carries over: no

| Action | Energy cost | Stat change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| High-intensity work | 2 | Output +, Health -, Dignity - |
| Skill learning | 2 | Skill +, Health - |
| Network maintenance | 1 | Network +, Dignity + |
| Defuse legacy risk | 2 | None (or an effect you cannot see) |
| Mental recovery | 1 | Dignity + |
| Health recovery | 1 | Health + |
| Prepare report materials | 1 | Output +, Dignity + |

## Main actions

Each quarter, pick one main action or none.

- Most you can pick each quarter: 1
- You may take no main action: yes

| Action | Stat change |
| --- | --- |
| Apply for a key project | Output +, Skill +, Network + |
| Report results to your manager | Output +, Network +, Dignity + |
| Fight for resources | Output +, Network + |
| Apply for rotation | Skill +, Network + |
| Showcase results | Output +, Dignity + |
| Build a mentorship | Skill +, Network + |
| Repair a key relationship | Network +, Dignity + |
| Lay low and reduce risk | Health + |

## Wealth and monthly pay

You are paid a base salary each month according to your level: 0.3 Wealth a month at L1, rising with each level to 9.1 a month at L10.

| Level | Monthly base (Wealth) |
| --- | --- |
| L1 | 0.3 |
| L2 | 0.4 |
| L3 | 0.5 |
| L4 | 0.7 |
| L5 | 1.0 |
| L6 | 1.5 |
| L7 | 2.3 |
| L8 | 3.6 |
| L9 | 5.7 |
| L10 | 9.1 |

## Performance review

- How often: Formal review every 6 months
- Note: Performance combines Skill, Network, Output, level, etc.; bonus is a multiple of base monthly pay. The bands are published in advance and applied the same way to everyone.

| Grade | Meaning | Bonus |
| --- | --- | --- |
| S | Exceptional | base monthly ×3 |
| A | Strong | base monthly ×2 |
| B | Solid | base monthly ×1 |
| C | Weak | base monthly ×0.25 |
| D | Very weak | no bonus |

## Risk and failure

The red lines are not in the onboarding slides. Old hands will tell you what tends to blow up. The timing and counts you learn by playing.

### What people say

- Old landmines all go off at once, and half a year of work vanishes!
- In a review your teammates use jargon you cannot keep up with. You nod and promise to look into it…

### Ways people say a run ends

- Blackout — your body gives out before the KPIs do. Game over
- Breakdown — after months with no dignity left, you send a resignation email
- Trust crisis — after a second blow-up, the company says you have used up its trust
- Dismissed for capability — two weak half-year reviews and you hand the badge in
- Isolated — work that needs other people cannot get done, and you resign
- Broke — months with an empty wallet
- Obsolete — your manager suggests a role that matches what you can actually do

Survive all 48 months and you may earn a career summary worth showing.'}

# Story option choice

## When to use
For every story event with two or more choices, after career-compass. The reading is internal, at most three short lines; the decision ends with take_action in the same turn.

- Drivers: Skill, Network and Output. Target: the driver career-compass named for this decision.

1. Read the event text and every option in full.
2. For each option, infer from its wording which visible statistics it raises or lowers. Handbook vocabulary: overtime, weekends, late nights, carrying two jobs and pushing through cost Health; learning and certification raise Skill and cost Health; helping, meeting, crediting or introducing people raises Network; delivering, presenting results or taking visible work raises Output; standing up for yourself protects Dignity; purchases and loans move Wealth. Two patterns from our runs, which outrank the vocabulary:
   - Options that put work or people down cost a driver even when they sound sensible: declining or deferring a request, keeping strictly to your hours, taking leave, rolling back, "leave it to them", "stay out of it", a private word instead of a public contribution, and "set the record straight with evidence". At the entry level these cost Network or Output in most cases.
   - Options that do the work together keep or raise the drivers: help in person, cover the urgent part, draft a joint plan and copy the manager, propose a process or a prototype, put data on the shared record, take the task within your hours.
3. Mark the options that bury hidden risk: staying silent or looking away; denying, lying or inventing a story; covering up a problem or hiding a health problem and pushing through; venting, sulking, threats or coasting in protest; favours and back channels; leaking, gossiping or blaming others; shortcuts, tweaked results and accepting a known safety or security flaw for later.
4. Remove, in this order: every marked option; every option that costs Health while Health is not healthy; every option that costs Dignity while Dignity is low; in the month before a review, every option that costs two or more points on one statistic or lowers two at once. If nothing is left, keep the option with the smallest damage that a quarterly action can repair, and write "risk flag" in the note.
5. Choose among the rest:
   - The option that raises the target with no cost to Health, Dignity or another driver.
   - Else the option that raises the target at a cost of one point of Health while Health is healthy, or one point of Dignity while Dignity is healthy.
   - Else the option that keeps every driver where it is; between equals, the one that puts you in the room with the manager or senior people, which counts as Network.
   - After a blow-up, or while the HR remark says the risks have piled up or worse: the option that owns the problem and puts it on the record.
   - If none of the above fits: the option with the smallest total cost among the remaining ones, counting a point of a driver and a point of Health or Dignity alike; between equals, the one a quarterly action can repair (Health, Dignity, Network, Output) rather than one it cannot (Wealth, hidden risk).

- Pressure to cut corners, hide a problem or inflate numbers: refuse, and raise it with your own manager first; go past the manager only when the manager is the problem.
- Your own mistake or a slipping deadline: own it at once, with a cause and a recovery plan. In our runs this lowered hidden risk; silence raised it.
- Credit or blame disputes: offer the joint fix in writing with the manager copied; the facts go on the shared record. Do not accept blame you do not own; do not fight it in the room.
- Declining: only what buries risk, costs Health while Health is not healthy, or breaks a rule. Decline with an alternative (a later date, a smaller scope, a hand-off), never with a flat no or a silent yes.
- Office politics, favour trading and campaigning: stay out; keep to the work and to the facts.

## Before take_action
Do not make large purchases or lend money when Wealth is low. Between two equal options take the one whose effect is clearest and easiest to reverse. Then call take_action, and observe once after it.

# Quarter plan

## When to use
When observe shows the quarterly Energy phase or the main-action choice, after career-compass. The plan is internal, at most three short lines; every decision ends with take_action in the same turn. At the quarterly phase after each half-year review (end of months 6, 12, 18 and so on), load the three Skills again before the first quarterly decision.

## Terms used in this Skill
- Drivers: Skill, Network and Output. Target: the driver career-compass named. Ceiling: a driver that did not rise across two quarterly phases although something was meant to raise it; nothing is spent on it until a promotion or until it drops.
- Healthy / watch / low: Health or Dignity at 7 or more / 4 to 6 / below 4 (our own bands).
- Defuse: the Energy action "Defuse legacy risk". - Stage: entry (no promotion yet), climb, senior (twelve months or more at the level after two promotions), final year (month 37 on), as career-compass set it.

## Procedure
1. Read the menu. Its status_updates and energy_cost give the exact effect and price of every action; use them, never memory. The same action may be chosen more than once within the three points.
2. The first take_action note of the phase states, from the ledger only: "<each driver: open or ceiling>; defuse <due or not due>; stage <name>".
3. Energy, in this order:
   1. Recovery to the band: Health low takes Health recovery until it is at least 4; Dignity low takes Mental recovery until it is at least 4. In the first quarterly phase of the run, and in any phase whose next three months include a review month, buy one Health recovery unless Health is already healthy: the review uses the state before the review month, so Health bought later arrives too late.
   2. Defuse legacy risk when a defuse is due.
   3. End of the run: at the end of months 45 and 48, the points left go to Health recovery and Mental recovery, the lower first, up to the top of each scale. Only points still left go on.
   4. Growth: the remaining points go to open drivers, the target first - Network maintenance for Network, Prepare report materials for Output, Skill learning for Skill only while Health is healthy. Senior stage and final year: Skill learning first while Skill is open and Health is healthy. High-intensity work is not used: its menu text lists a Health and Dignity cost and a hidden-risk effect, and Prepare report materials raises Output without them.
   5. All drivers at their ceiling: Health recovery and Mental recovery up to healthy, then a defuse if none this quarter, then Skill learning while Health is healthy. Leave a point unspent only when nothing above can use it; the menu says unused Energy does not carry over.
4. Main action, the first rule that applies:
   1. Health low, the first two quarters after a blow-up, or the HR remark at "piled up" or worse: Lay low and reduce risk.
   2. Dignity low, or Network at zero: Repair a key relationship.
   3. Entry stage: Build a mentorship when Network is the target (its menu effect raises Network most), otherwise Apply for a key project.
   4. Senior stage and final year while Skill is open: Apply for rotation (its menu effect raises Skill and Network); if two windows at this level passed without a promotion while rotation was the main action, Apply for a key project instead.

   6. Otherwise, in every quarter including the one before a review: Apply for a key project, because its menu effect raises all three drivers at once.
   7. End of month 48: Build a mentorship if Network is open, otherwise Lay low and reduce risk.
5. Every other take_action note in the phase is one sentence: the action, the driver it serves and "expect <statistic> <+n or -n>".

## Wealth
No Energy action or main action raises Wealth directly; it comes from the monthly salary of the level and the half-year bonus, which the grade sets. A Wealth that is flat or negative is therefore answered by the plan above - growth on the target for the next review, no large purchase or loan in story events - and never by skipping recovery or a due defuse.

## Check before each take_action
- Nothing on a driver at its ceiling except Skill learning in step 3.5; no recovery past the top of a scale; no Skill learning or High-intensity work while Health is not healthy.
- A defuse due this phase is in the plan before any growth point.
- Months 45 and 48: recovery before growth.
- After take_action, observe once.

# Career compass

## When to use
At every decision point, right after observe has returned the current state. The compass is internal reasoning, at most three short lines; every decision ends with a tool call in the same turn.

## Terms used in this Skill
- Drivers: Skill, Network and Output, the three visible statistics the handbook names for promotion.
- Healthy / watch / low: Health or Dignity at 7 or more / 4 to 6 / below 4. Our own planning bands, not game thresholds.

## Procedure
1. Read from the observe result only: month, level and months at level, the nine visible statistics, the monthly feed (salary, HR remark, review grade, promotion, warnings) and your own last note. Never use a value from memory.
2. Set the stage from the level and the calendar, in this order:
   - Final year: month 37 or later. Promotions still happen at months 42 and 48; the ending evaluation also counts Skill, Network, Wealth, Health, Dignity and risk control.
   - Entry: no promotion yet. In our runs the windows at months 6 and 12 decided the whole run; a career still at the first level after month 12 seldom recovered.
   - Senior: twelve months or more at the current level after at least two promotions. In our runs the upper levels asked for much more Skill and more months at the level than the lower ones.
   - Climb: everything else.
3. Ledger of the drivers. For each driver write open or ceiling:
   - Ceiling: the value did not rise across the last two quarterly phases although Energy, a main action or a story result was meant to raise it. One flat quarter is not enough.
   - A driver at its ceiling becomes open again after a promotion, or when it drops below the value it stuck at (then it is open until it is back there).
   - Judge "behind" by movement and room, never by raw size: Skill is naturally several times larger than Network and Output at every level, so a large Skill is not "ahead".
4. Target: the open driver that rose least over the last quarter. Entry stage: all three must reach their ceiling before the end of month 5 and again before the end of month 11, so the target is whichever driver is still moving. Senior stage and final year: Skill, as long as it is open and Health is healthy; otherwise the open driver that rose least.
5. Repair check, which overrides the target when it applies:
   - Health or Dignity low: recovery first, and no option or action that costs it.
   - Health in watch: growth only through options that cost no Health.
   - Wealth negative, or Network at zero: raise it before anything else; the handbook lists both as failure directions when they persist.

In our runs it moved in steps from calm ("doing all right") to alarm ("about to go off"); read it as a direction, not as a number.    - Calendar: in the month before a review, no option that costs two or more points on one statistic or lowers two at once.
6. Expectation check: compare the expectation written in your last note with what actually changed. On a miss, add one short lesson to the next note naming the kind of option and its real effect, never an event by name. Lessons in your notes outrank the general reading rules in story-option-choice.

Stage; open drivers and ceilings; target; repair items that apply; months to the next review.

## Priorities near a limit
- Health or Dignity low in two observations in a row outranks everything.

   - Entry: no promotion yet. In our runs the windows at months 6 and 12 decided the whole run; a career still at the first level after month 12 seldom recovered.
   - Senior: twelve months or more at the current level after at least two promotions. In our runs the upper levels asked for much more Skill and more months at the level than the lower ones.
   - Climb: everything else.
3. Ledger of the drivers. For each driver write open or ceiling:
   - Ceiling: the value did not rise across the last two quarterly phases although Energy, a main action or a story result was meant to raise it. One flat quarter is not enough.
   - A driver at its ceiling becomes open again after a promotion, or when it drops below the value it stuck at (then it is open until it is back there).
   - Judge "behind" by movement and room, never by raw size: Skill is naturally several times larger than Network and Output at every level, so a large Skill is not "ahead".
4. Target: the open driver that rose least over the last quarter. Entry stage: all three must reach their ceiling before the end of month 5 and again before the end of month 11, so the target is whichever driver is still moving. Senior stage and final year: Skill, as long as it is open and Health is healthy; otherwise the open driver that rose least.
5. Repair check, which overrides the target when it applies:
   - Health or Dignity low: recovery first, and no option or action that costs it.
   - Health in watch: growth only through options that cost no Health.
   - Wealth negative, or Network at zero: raise it before anything else; the handbook lists both as failure directions when they persist.
   - Hidden risk: the handbook does not publish it, so read the HR remark in the monthly feed as a gauge. In our runs it moved in steps from calm ("doing all right") to alarm ("about to go off"); read it as a direction, not as a number. A remark that says the risks have piled up or worse, or a story that came back after a silent, hidden or shortcut choice, means a defuse is due at the next quarterly phase. After a blow-up (the feed reports that buried risks have gone off), the next two quarters add no new risk and defuse once; this is our own policy, since the published failure directions say a serious consequence can follow accumulated risk.
   - Calendar: in the month before a review, no option that costs two or more points on one statistic or lowers two at once.
6. Expectation check: compare the expectation written in your last note with what actually changed. On a miss, add one short lesson to the next note naming the kind of option and its real effect, never an event by name. Lessons in your notes outrank the general reading rules in story-option-choice.

## Output (internal, two or three lines)
Stage; open drivers and ceilings; target; repair items that apply; months to the next review.

## Priorities near a limit
- Health or Dignity low in two observations in a row outranks everything.
- After a C or D grade: for the next two quarters every story choice and Energy point goes to the target, through options that cost no Health; one more weak review can end the run.
- Two windows at the same level without a promotion: change the main-action pattern in quarter-plan instead of repeating it.
- Output is needed for promotion but is not part of the ending evaluation; Skill and Network are both. From the senior stage on, Skill is raised first.
